title: Throughput variance containment and runbook for autoscaler-feedback divergence
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: A production incident was triggered by a sudden variance in per-pool throughput and tail-latency that coincided with an autoscaler-feedback divergence. The autoscaler decision loop began to oscillate after a runtime kernel-selection change and a drift in the headroom predictor. Impact: several Dedicated customers observed degraded throughput and increased 95th/99th latency for 18 minutes across two GPU pools. Important: traffic routing and SLAs were at risk; we applied emergency containment to avoid larger SLA breaches. 

Timeline: 
- 2026-02-10 09:13 UTC: Alerting detected >30% decrease in sustained per-GPU token throughput for pool-us-east-3. Grafana alerted on combined metric "dedicated.pool.throughput_variance" and increased queue depth. 
- 09:17 UTC: On-call acknowledged and opened this ticket. 
- 09:22 UTC: Emergency throttles applied on new-route consumers; burst policy disabled for affected pools. 
- 09:29 UTC: Autoscaler showed repeated scale-ups and scale-downs (oscillation) due to stale headroom and a new kernel selection that changed latency distributions. 
- 09:34 UTC: Rolled back autoscaler config to pinned version from 2026-02-05 and re-enabled legacy kernel selector for the affected model family. Throughput normalized by 09:41 UTC. 

Immediate mitigation performed: 
- Temporary per-customer rate caps applied for top 5 impacted customers (identifiers redacted). 
- Deployed autoscaler config rollback (git PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/compare/rollback-2026-02) 
- Re-enabled legacy kernel selection for model variants with recent kernel changes. 
- Increased headroom reserve for pool-us-east-3 by 12% (manual override). 
- Triggered manual rebalancing job to redistribute KV-cache-heavy load across healthy nodes. 

Root cause (preliminary): 
- A low-latency-optimized kernel selection change reduced per-request variance for short sequences but introduced a small increase in peak memory footprint for mid-length contexts. The headroom predictor did not account for this shift, returning over-optimistic available capacity values. 
- The autoscaler feedback loop used a smoothed metric that suppressed the early spike signals; when the oscillation started, cooldown windows and smoothing amplified the oscillation instead of damping it. 
- Telemetry for kernel-selection-induced memory impact was absent from the autoscaler inputs. 

Short-term action items (all owners assigned below): 
- AUTO-1 (Ravi P): Harden autoscaler circuit breaker to break on sustained oscillation pattern >3 cycles (deadline 2026-03-01). 
- TELE-1 (Maya G): Add kernel memory-pressure metric to autoscaler inputs and expose in Grafana (deadline 2026-03-05). 
- RUNBOOK-1 (SRE team): Publish a dedicated runbook page for throughput-variance containment and include rollback checklist (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/throughput-variance-runbook) (deadline 2026-03-08). 
- QA-1 (QAE team): Create a canary traffic test that exercises kernel-selection permutations under KV-cache pressure (estimate 5 points). 

Long-term roadmap items: 
- Replace smoothed single-window scaling signal with multi-timescale anomaly detector to prevent under-reacting to early spikes. 
- Instrument kernel selector to emit expected memory multiplier per model variant; feed into headroom predictor. 
- Add synthetic load tests that combine prefix caching hot-paths with long-context requests to validate autoscaler stability. 

Acceptance criteria for done: 
- Autoscaler no longer oscillates under similar workload patterns in staging canary runs. 
- Runbook reviewed and runbook drill executed with on-call rotation. 
- Grafana dashboards display kernel-memory impact and a new "autoscaler-health" panel. 

Notes about trade-offs and decisions: 
- We chose rollback + increased headroom rather than an immediate kernel revert to minimize risk to other regions that had seen performance improvements from the kernel change. Rollback of autoscaler config was faster to apply and less likely to cause regressions in unrelated pools. 
- We will accept a small short-term increase in cost (reserve headroom) to preserve SLA and get telemetry improved before a full kernel rollback.
